week_in_brief: Rates at 6.94%, internal recruiting outpacing external by 52%, and Clear Cooperation back under review—a week of structural uncertainty.

items.headline: Mortgage Rates Hit 6.94%, Deal-Making Now Premium Skill
items.whats_happening: 30-year rates climbed from 6.23% in February to 6.94% this week as Iran conflict tension destabilizes markets. Brokers project ~400K lost sales nationally for 2026—sellers are pulling listings, buyers are fewer but negotiating from strength, and discounts aren't closing the gap. Buydowns and phased pricing are replacing price cuts.
items.so_what: Shift marketing dollars from volume campaigns to recruiting and retaining skilled agents who can structure creative deals. This is an expertise market—your best producers are your best advertising.

items.headline: Recruiting Wars Are Dead, Internal Transfers Are Up 52%
items.whats_happening: Q2 data shows external brand switches essentially flat year-over-year while internal transfers surged 52% to 800 moves. Internal movers carry 31% higher median production. Only 2.92% of productive agents switched brands. The recruiting report warns brokers to shift from "land grab" to precision targeting of top 10% producers and vulnerable small-to-mid-size teams.
items.so_what: If your recruiting pitch is still "join us and grow," you're fighting yesterday's battle. Focus retention on your top 10% and build co-branded marketing infrastructure that keeps them from walking. That's your competitive moat now.

items.headline: CRMLS Surveys 27K Agents on Clear Cooperation; MLS Governance Under Pressure
items.whats_happening: California Regional MLS distributed a survey to 27,000+ active users to assess industry perspectives on Clear Cooperation Policy—the MLS rule requiring timely public listing disclosure. Results will inform policy and governance decisions. This comes as Zillow/Compass/MRED litigation continues and national-scale MLS consolidation creates new data control dynamics.
items.so_what: If you're depending on portal visibility for buyer leads, pay attention. MLS governance fights and national consolidation (Compass now owns the feed for Coldwell Banker, Sotheby's, and more) could compress your reach. Invest now in owned organic search and direct buyer relationships as a hedge.

items.headline: AI Passage Optimization Beats Traditional SEO for Citations
items.whats_happening: A year-long study of 15.7 million Google AI Mode citations found that 47.7% were formatted as scroll-to-text highlights, not plain links. Pages with 21+ highlighted passages achieved median #1 rankings. This signals a fundamental shift: AI search rewards passage quality and structure over traditional on-page metrics.
items.so_what: Restructure your brokerage content and agent pages to lead with self-contained answers in full paragraphs—"What's the average time on market in [ZIP]?" gets a direct answer, not an intro paragraph. AI citations are the new lead gen channel; your pages need to be written for machines first, humans second.

this_weeks_take: The fundamentals are shifting faster than most brokerages are adjusting. Rates are up, recruiting is local, MLS rules are under review, and AI is rewriting how buyers find agents. The winners will be the brokerages that stop chasing last year's playbook and start building for the market that's actually here.
